column2: folded step 6 stdout will prefix check-change kvs (`files_changed`, `untracked_baseline`, `git_probe_failed`) before the checks relay line, but the plan leaves first-physical-line `redacted_log_file` parsing unchanged. on `next_action=checks-failed` the first line may be `files_changed=...`, so the checks failure entry macro and step 6 prose never see `redacted_log_file` and the step 6 repair loop cannot start.

folding both step 6 legs into one immediate-background `step-6-entry.sh` fence without relocating the canonical `> **continue after child returns.**` opener leaves the skip-to-7a path (and other routes) without the anti-halt contract `test-implement-relevant-checks-anti-halt.sh` enforces within five preceding lines. the harness currently matches only `checks-commit-route`/`checks-step5-resume` and may not accept `next_action=skip-to-7a` as valid success guidance.

the `step6_entry_main` rewrite omits the required `--baseline pre-review-untracked.txt` and `--head-baseline pre-review-head.txt` argv contract. today's shell and python forward paths pass both; a generic captured check-changes call can miss review-phase untracked/head movement and emit `files_changed=false` after review edits.

the planned step 6 skill edit narrows the invalid-envelope contract. live prose treats missing/duplicate/malformed `next_action`, seed-failed commit-route seeding, and non-zero output without `next_action` as one path with warnings logging, `stall_tracking=true`, `stall_step=7` when durable seed is absent, and skip to step 18. the plan revision only mentions malformed `next_action`, so implementers may drop seed-failed and non-zero-without-`next_action` handling and stall or route at the wrong step.

the plan moves the prompt-facing step 6 machine envelope from `review-and-fix check-changes` to `implement step-6-entry` but does not add `("implement", "step-6-entry")` to `_machine_stdout_keys`. without registration, inherited quiet routing may not be disabled for the entrypoint that now emits `files_changed`, `checkpoint_next`, and `next_action`, so the orchestrator can miss the composite routing envelope.

today section 2/4 of `checks-repair-loop.md` re-runs `checks-commit-route --checks-site step6`, which always executes the checks leg. the plan retargets re-entry to `step-6-entry.sh`, which runs `check-changes` first and emits `next_action=skip-to-7a` when `files_changed=false`. after a checks failure plus repair, a tree that no longer differs from pre-review baselines (full revert, probe degradation, or baseline drift) can route to step 7a without re-running step6 checks.

the planned `test_composite_outer_timeout_budgets_match_leg_sums_and_fences` launcher pin will not match the planned `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh` timeout tuple. the plan repoints the step 6 timeout pin to `skills/implement/scripts/step-6-entry.sh --forked-target "${forked_target:-false}"` but updates `step6_launcher` to only `skills/implement/scripts/step-6-entry.sh`. the test asserts that exact `(launcher + '<step6_launcher>', 'timeout: …')` literal exists in `test-implement-structure.sh`; with the longer tuple in structure, the substring match fails and ci breaks even when the fold is otherwise correct.

step 6 `--force-checks true` repair re-entry is scoped only to section 4 `next_action=continue`; `main-agent-edit` still mandates identical argv. the plan adds `--force-checks true` only under section 4 `next_action=continue`. section 4 `main-agent-edit` still tells the orchestrator to re-run the section 2 launcher with identical argv (lines 77 and 81). after a step 6 checks failure, lint-fix may route `main-agent-edit`; once repair edits restore pre-review baselines, a normal `step-6-entry.sh` re-entry can emit `next_action=skip-to-7a` and bypass the step 6 checks/commit/7.r composite without re-running checks.
